extracted_claims.text: Article 43 establishes two conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or assessment of quality management system plus technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII.

For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometric identification systems), the provider may choose internal control (Annex VI) or notified body assessment (Annex VII) depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied.

Annex VII (notified body) assessment is mandatory for biometric identification systems and certain critical infrastructure AI systems; most other high-risk AI systems can use the Annex VI self-assessment route.

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU product-safety legislation in Annex I Section A (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the conformity assessment procedures of that legislation, with notified bodies also verifying compliance with the AI-specific requirements.

Providers may choose any notified body for the Annex VII procedure, except that where the high-risk AI system is to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities or Union institutions, the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body.
Substantial modifications to a high-risk AI system require a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in systems designed to continue learning after deployment.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority, by derogation from Article 43, to authorise placing on the market or putting into service of a specific high-risk AI system without the standard conformity assessment, for exceptional reasons of public security, health, environmental protection or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets, for a limited period.

Annex VII section 4.5 provides that a notified body may, as a last resort and upon reasoned request, be granted access to the training and trained models of the AI system, including relevant parameters, to assess conformity with Chapter III Section 2 requirements, subject to IP and confidentiality protections.

Article 44 covers certificates, Article 45 covers information obligations of notified bodies, Article 47 covers the EU declaration of conformity, and Article 48 covers CE marking, as part of the Standards, Conformity Assessment, Certificates, Registration section of the AI Act.
Article 43(5) gives the European Commission power to adopt delegated acts to update Annex VI and Annex VII in light of technical progress, without needing to revise the AI Act itself.
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes rules on identification numbers and lists of notified bodies.
As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing across Member States and capacity described as limited.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act (in the medical devices/SaMD context).

Post-2026, notified bodies designated under the AI Act are expected to begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments, intersecting with existing MDR/IVDR notified body assessments for medical device AI.

As of October 2025, the NANDO system listed 51 MDR-designated notified bodies and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies (under the Medical Devices Regulation framework, not AI Act-specific designations).

A Council document (ST-7322-2026) references a classification system (AIP codes) for AI systems subject to Annex I, used to define the scope of designation of conformity assessment bodies notified under Article 30 of the relevant regulation (apparently the Machinery/other product regulation context).

A Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) proposes creating a new Annex XIV listing codes and categories of AI systems for the Commission's NANDO information system, and includes amendments to Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements, plus rules on entry into force.

High-risk AI obligations under Annex III were originally reported to apply from 2 December 2027, but one source reports this deadline was moved to 2 August 2029 under a final text agreed in September 2026, due to unreadiness of harmonised standards and notified bodies.
Another source states that from August 2026, high-risk AI obligations fully apply, calling it the key deadline for medical device AI (SaMD) compliance.
The EU AI Act declaration of conformity obligations, including Article 43 procedure references, were stated to be required before August 2, 2026 for SaaS providers.

For the Cyber Resilience Act (a related but separate regulation), as of late June 2026 zero notified bodies had been designated in the Commission's NANDO database, with a target of 11 December 2026 for sufficient notified body capacity and full application from 11 December 2027.

open_issues: No official EU source among those provided confirms whether any notified bodies have actually been designated specifically under the EU AI Act (as opposed to MDR/IVDR or other frameworks) as of the current date (October 2026).

The exact, currently legally binding deadline for high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III is unclear given conflicting claims (August 2026 vs. December 2027 vs. August 2029) and the sources are a mix of undated blogs and unverified claims about a 'final text agreed in September 2026' that is not corroborated by any official EU source in this set.

The full text and final adopted status of COM(2025) 836 and its proposed Annex XIV / NANDO classification system is not confirmed — sources only describe it as a 'proposal' without indicating whether it has been adopted.

It is unclear how many notified bodies, if any, have completed the AI-Act-specific designation process under Article 43/Annex VII as opposed to being designated only under MDR/IVDR or other sectoral legislation.

The relationship between the Council document's AIP coding system (source 8) and the official Annex XIV proposal (source 9) is not fully clarified — whether they refer to the same instrument or a different implementing framework.

The interplay and sequencing between MDR/IVDR notified body assessments and new AI Act notified body assessments for medical device AI remains only partially described, without clear procedural detail on how a single product would undergo both assessments.
No source clarifies whether the Commission has exercised its Article 43(5) delegated act power to update Annexes VI or VII as of the current date.
report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures and Notified Bodies for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes two main conformity assessment pathways for high-risk AI systems — internal control (Annex VI) and notified body assessment (Annex VII) — with the applicable route depending on the system's category and whether harmonised standards exist (low confidence to high confidence, varying by claim) ([VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). However, the notified body ecosystem specifically for AI Act purposes appears largely undeveloped as of 2026, with conflicting and low-confidence reports on both designation progress and the applicable compliance deadlines.

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 establishes two conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system plus technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) ([VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai), [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)). For systems in point 1 of Annex III (biometric identification), the provider may choose between internal control and notified body assessment depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf)). One interpretation suggests Annex VII assessment is mandatory for biometric identification and certain critical infrastructure systems, while most other high-risk systems may use Annex VI self-assessment (low confidence) ([Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)).

For high-risk AI systems already covered by existing EU product-safety legislation (Annex I Section A, e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow that sectoral legislation's conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)).

### Procedural Details
Providers may generally choose any notified body for the Annex VII procedure, except where the system is to be used by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions — in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Substantial modifications to a high-risk system require a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in continuously-learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits derogation from standard assessment for exceptional public security, health, environmental, or infrastructure reasons, for a limited period (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Annex VII section 4.5 allows notified bodies, as a last resort, to access training data and models to verify compliance, subject to IP protections (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)). Related articles cover certificates (Art. 44), notified body information obligations (Art. 45), the EU declaration of conformity (Art. 47), and CE marking (Art. 48) (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-60)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
As of October 2025, the NANDO system listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies — figures relevant to medical-device AI but not specific to the AI Act (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). Separately, a Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) would create a new Annex XIV listing AI system codes/categories for the NANDO database and amend Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 (medium confidence) ([Council document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)), while a related Council document references an "AIP code" classification system for designating conformity assessment bodies (medium confidence) ([Council document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). Lower-confidence sources indicate the AI Act-specific notified body ecosystem remained under construction as of March 2026 (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)), with one source claiming zero formal AI Act designations as of April 2026 (low confidence) ([AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources sharply disagree on the binding deadline for high-risk obligations: one low-confidence, uncorroborated blog claims a shift to 2 August 2029 ([AI Act news blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)), while another states obligations fully apply from August 2026 ([MDXcro](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd)) — neither is confirmed by an official EU source. Similarly, reports conflict on whether any AI Act notified bodies exist: "zero designations" versus "ongoing" processes (both low confidence) ([AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide); [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). The Commission's delegated act power under Article 43(5) to update Annexes VI/VII is noted but unverified in current application (low confidence) ([FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether any notified bodies have been formally designated specifically under the AI Act (versus MDR/IVDR), the true legally binding deadline for Annex III obligations, the adoption status of COM(2025) 836 and Annex XIV, and how AI Act and MDR/IVDR assessments will be sequenced for a single product. Further official EU confirmation (e.g., via NANDO) is needed.

# Conformity Assessment Procedures and Notified Bodies for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes two main conformity assessment pathways for high-risk AI systems — internal control (Annex VI) and notified body assessment (Annex VII) — with the applicable route depending on the system's category and whether harmonised standards exist (low confidence to high confidence, varying by claim) ([VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). However, the notified body ecosystem specifically for AI Act purposes appears largely undeveloped as of 2026, with conflicting and low-confidence reports on both designation progress and the applicable compliance deadlines.

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 establishes two conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system plus technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) ([VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai), [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)). For systems in point 1 of Annex III (biometric identification), the provider may choose between internal control and notified body assessment depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf)). One interpretation suggests Annex VII assessment is mandatory for biometric identification and certain critical infrastructure systems, while most other high-risk systems may use Annex VI self-assessment (low confidence) ([Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)).

For high-risk AI systems already covered by existing EU product-safety legislation (Annex I Section A, e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow that sectoral legislation's conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)).

### Procedural Details
Providers may generally choose any notified body for the Annex VII procedure, except where the system is to be used by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions — in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Substantial modifications to a high-risk system require a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in continuously-learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits derogation from standard assessment for exceptional public security, health, environmental, or infrastructure reasons, for a limited period (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Annex VII section 4.5 allows notified bodies, as a last resort, to access training data and models to verify compliance, subject to IP protections (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)). Related articles cover certificates (Art. 44), notified body information obligations (Art. 45), the EU declaration of conformity (Art. 47), and CE marking (Art. 48) (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-60)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
As of October 2025, the NANDO system listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies — figures relevant to medical-device AI but not specific to the AI Act (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). Separately, a Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) would create a new Annex XIV listing AI system codes/categories for the NANDO database and amend Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 (medium confidence) ([Council document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)), while a related Council document references an "AIP code" classification system for designating conformity assessment bodies (medium confidence) ([Council document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). Lower-confidence sources indicate the AI Act-specific notified body ecosystem remained under construction as of March 2026 (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)), with one source claiming zero formal AI Act designations as of April 2026 (low confidence) ([AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources sharply disagree on the binding deadline for high-risk obligations: one low-confidence, uncorroborated blog claims a shift to 2 August 2029 ([AI Act news blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)), while another states obligations fully apply from August 2026 ([MDXcro](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd)) — neither is confirmed by an official EU source. Similarly, reports conflict on whether any AI Act notified bodies exist: "zero designations" versus "ongoing" processes (both low confidence) ([AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide); [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). The Commission's delegated act power under Article 43(5) to update Annexes VI/VII is noted but unverified in current application (low confidence) ([FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether any notified bodies have been formally designated specifically under the AI Act (versus MDR/IVDR), the true legally binding deadline for Annex III obligations, the adoption status of COM(2025) 836 and Annex XIV, and how AI Act and MDR/IVDR assessments will be sequenced for a single product. Further official EU confirmation (e.g., via NANDO) is needed.
